extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: A widely used machine learning dataset used to train and evaluate neural networks, including a test set for measuring accuracy.
extraction.creator: Krizhevsky et al.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper does not describe collecting new data; it uses the existing CIFAR-10 dataset for training and evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source data are CIFAR-10 images: 60,000 32x32 color images labeled into ten classes, split into 50,000 training images and 10,000 validation/test images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The methods are optimized specifically for CIFAR-10 under fixed performance and hardware constraints, and horizontal flipping is not universally beneficial across tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training and benchmarking image classification methods on CIFAR-10, with released scripts targeting different accuracy/speed tradeoffs; one compiled variant is intended for experiments where many networks are trained at once.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code is released publicly as the airbench Python package / GitHub repository, but no update schedule, maintainer details, or deprecation policy are specified.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation with random horizontal flipping and 2-pixel random translation during training; test-time augmentation using horizontal flipping and multi-crop evaluation; proposed derandomized alternating flip variant of horizontal flipping.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For translation augmentation, images are reflection-padded by 2 pixels and then a random 32x32 crop is taken.

name.evidence: CIFAR-10 is among the most widely used datasets in machine learning

description.evidence: CIFAR-10 is among the most widely used datasets in machine learning, facilitating thousands of research projects per year... Our objective is to develop a training method which reaches 94% accuracy on the CIFAR-10 test-set

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky et al., 2009) is one of the most popular datasets in machine learning”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We developed airbench solely with the goal of maximizing training speed on CIFAR-10... These constraints mean that we cannot improve performance by simply scaling up the amount of computational resources used... We note that, surprisingly to us, the standard ImageNet trainings that we considered do not significantly benefit from horizontal flipping.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To accelerate research and reduce the cost of experiments, we introduce training methods for CIFAR-10... We release the following methods in total. 1. airbench94_compiled.py... 2. airbench94.py... 3. airbench95.py... 4. airbench96.py... It is intended for experiments where many networks are trained at once in order to amortize the one-time compilation cost.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: Our code is released at https://github.com/KellerJordan/cifar10-airbench... It is released as the airbench Python package.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “For data augmentation we use random horizontal flipping alongside 2-pixel random translation.” ; “During evaluation we use horizontal flipping test-time augmentation” ; “To generate predictions, we run the trained network on six augmented views of each test image” ; “we propose a derandomized variant of standard horizontal flipping augmentation”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “For translation we use reflection padding ... Note that what we call 2-pixel random translation is equivalent to padding with 2 pixels and then taking a random 32x32 crop.”
